status: DRAFT — English rendering of the sealed French questions (plain-questions.v1.json). Same atoms, same quantifier words. To be read by a context-free English reader for leading wording before use; results from English-speaking raters are tagged by language and reported separately.
rule: One question per atom the verifier evaluates. The quantifier word is in the question: EVERY for forall and forall_exists, NO for not_exists, singular wording for exists. A question never names the expected answer.

questions.ac.a1: Does the student say clearly which option they choose?
questions.ac.a2: Does the chosen option fit what the assignment asked for: the right people, the right target, the right situation, the right time frame?
questions.ac.a3: Does the answer tell the intended person what to choose or do, without having to guess between materially different actions?
questions.ca.a1: Is EVERY calculation in the comparison correct?
questions.ca.a2: In EVERY calculation, are the units consistent with each other?
questions.ca.a3: Do the things being compared cover the same scope, according to the file?
questions.cf.a1: Is EVERY useful claim in this passage consistent with the file?
questions.cf.a2: For EVERY useful claim in this passage, does the student state a limit that bounds it?
questions.cf.a3: For EVERY useful claim, is the stated limit correct, according to the file?
questions.dp.a1: Does the student clearly state a position?
questions.dp.a2: Does the position tell the intended person what to choose or do, without having to guess between materially different actions?
questions.dp.a3: Does the position fit what the assignment asked for: the right people, the right object, the right situation, the right time frame?
questions.esg.a1: Does the student describe a sequence, that is, a chain of steps or events?
questions.esg.a2: Does that sequence rest on observations from the file?
questions.ff.a2: Is EVERY fact or figure put forward accurate, according to the file?
questions.ff.a3: Is EVERY fact or figure put forward related to the choice the student made, given the assignment?
questions.ff.a4: Does EVERY fact or figure put forward support the choice the student made?
questions.ml.a1: Does the student state a mechanism or a conclusion?
questions.ml.a2: Is EVERY fact cited explicitly linked to that mechanism or conclusion?
questions.pe.a1: Does the student produce evidence that can be checked?
questions.pe.a2: Does that evidence demonstrate the practice the assignment asked for?
questions.pe.a3: Is the student’s reading of that evidence correct, according to the file?
questions.rl.a1: Does the student clearly state the reflective link the assignment asked for?
questions.rl.a2: Does that link rest on a concrete element of the answer?
questions.rr.a1: Does the student name a risk?
questions.rr.a2: Does that risk remain after the proposed action?
questions.rr.a3: Is that risk both accurate AND relevant, according to the file?
questions.rr.a4: Does the student propose a precaution?
questions.rr.a5: Does that precaution reduce that risk?
questions.rr.a6: Is that precaution proportionate to that risk, according to the file?
questions.sfu.a1: Does EVERY fact used come from the scenario in the file?
questions.sfu.a2: Is EVERY fact used accurate, according to the file?
questions.sfu.a3: Does EVERY fact used serve to answer what the assignment asked?
questions.sf.a1: Is EVERY fact from the file that the explanation needs restated in the answer?
questions.sf.a2: Is it true that NO important claim in the answer goes beyond the file?
questions.ub.a1: Does the student name an uncertainty?
questions.ub.a2: Is that uncertainty related to what the assignment asked?
questions.ub.a3: Is that uncertainty correctly delimited, according to the file?
questions.ub.a4: Despite that uncertainty, does the student take a proportionate decision?

glossary.according to the file / consistent with: consistent with what the file says or reasonably lets you infer; not a word-for-word quote, and never judged against knowledge from outside the file.
glossary.goes beyond the file: adds to the given facts, whether wrong or merely unverifiable.
glossary.comes from the scenario: written in the file as such, or clearly inferable; not a plausible guess.
glossary.useful / important claim: a claim that carries weight in the reasoning, not a linking sentence.
glossary.related to the choice: speaks about the decision the student made, even without proving it. « Serves to answer the assignment » and « related to the assignment » point at the task set, with the same latitude: a real link, not merely the same topic.
glossary.supports the choice: actually backs the decision taken; a fact can be on topic without proving anything, or even cut against it.
glossary.reflective link: the student connects their answer to their own process or experience, as the assignment asks.
glossary.proportionate: neither too weak nor excessive for the seriousness of what is at stake.
glossary.time frame: the period concerned: short or long term.
glossary.scope: what each compared item includes: same elements, same period.
glossary.intended person: who the advice is addressed to in the task, not the student.
glossary.correct (calculation): right in the mathematical sense, not fair.
glossary.units: units of measurement: euros, percentages, hours…
glossary.a limit that bounds a claim: a caveat or condition: « true unless… », « only in this case… ».
glossary.delimited (uncertainty): its outline is framed: neither too vague nor more precise than the file allows.
glossary.target / object: what the option or position is about: the thing to decide; the « intended person » is who the advice is for.
glossary.option / position: two words for two exercises: « option » when the student picks among proposed solutions, « position » when they take a stand. Same demand for clarity.
glossary.relevant: counts for what is at stake: the choice, the assignment or the file depending on the question. Same latitude everywhere: a real link, not merely the same topic.
glossary.accurate AND relevant (risk): yes only if both hold; no as soon as one fails, and say which in « why ».
glossary.evidence that can be checked: something a third party could verify against the file: a fact, a figure, a precise reference; not a general statement.
glossary.concrete element of the answer: a precise detail present in the student’s answer, not in the file: a fact, an example, a step.
glossary.mechanism: an explained chain of cause and consequence, not a physical device.
glossary.needed by the explanation: a fact from the file without which the explanation does not hold; judged by you, not by the student.
glossary.rests on observations from the file: drawn from what the file says or reasonably lets you infer; not a word-for-word quote.
